title: Operator tombstone reconciliation and safe-replay for on-prem upgrade failures
creator: Arielle Cheng
description:
Summary:
During a staged operator upgrade for several private/VPC tenants we observed a class of failures where the operator's internal garbage-collector/tombstone sweeper removed transient CRs and KV state that the post-upgrade reconcile expected to find. This led to tenant control loops entering a hard-to-recover state (reconcile loops with repeated 409/404s, helm post-upgrade hooks failing, and stalled nodeagent attachments). Multiple customers escalated with production traffic impacted and delayed rollouts.

Observed behavior:
- Helm upgrade returns success but subsequent operator reconcile fails with 404 on ephemeral CRs (eg. agent-attachment-<tenant>) and 409 on CR update attempts.
- Operator tombstone/GC runs during the upgrade window and finalizer removal race causes the resource to be deleted before the reconciler can rehydrate it.
- KV cache schema migration path expects a snapshot marker that was GC'd, causing manifest parity checks to fail and blocking further reconciles.
- Affected tenants: 6 customer clusters across two data regions; 3 escalations open with SEs.

Impact:
- Customer-facing control plane features temporarily degraded (autoscaling policies and rollout controllers blocked).
- Some dedicated customers required manual operator restarts and manual reapply of CRs to recover.

Root cause hypothesis:
- The upgrade sequencing allowed the operator GC controller to sweep objects created by pre-upgrade hooks while the post-upgrade reconciliation assumed those objects would persist until migration completed.
- The reconcile logic lacks idempotent replay for missing tombstoned resources and lacks a tombstone-reconciliation step to re-create necessary markers if safely possible.

Proposed solution (phased):
Phase 0 (emergency mitigation):
- Ship operator-2026.03-hotfix-01 that disables tombstone GC during the upgrade window for tenants flagged as 'in-progress'. This is a safe stop-gap to prevent further deletions.
- Add an automated check in the onprem upgrade sequencer to ensure GC controller is quiesced before helm preflight completes.

Phase 1 (short-term fix):
- Add a safe-replay reconciler subroutine: on reconcile failure due to missing ephemeral CRs or missing migration markers, attempt a bounded replay that re-creates ephemeral CRs with annotations indicating they were replayed by operator, and avoid overwriting existing finalizers.
- Add preflight post-hook: capture a per-tenant 'snapshot-marker' in the KV store that is treated as a durable anchor; the migration will not proceed if marker is absent.

Phase 2 (long-term):
- Implement tombstone reconciliation logic that can reconcile GC'd resources by consulting Helm release history + operator audit log and rehydrate without violating ownerReferences or causing duplicate resources.
- Tighten ordering guarantees: operator upgrade will now support an explicit 'quiesce' API that Helm hooks can call to pause GC and leader election during the upgrade window.

Testing and validation:
- Add unit tests for replay reconciler and integration tests for upgrade sequences that simulate mid-upgrade GC sweeps.
- Run chaos experiments in staging where we intentionally GC ephemeral CRs at multiple points in the upgrade and verify safe-replay recovers cluster to a stable state.

Rollout plan and customer communication:
- Hotfix rollout (operator-2026.03-hotfix-01) to affected customers within 24 hours; coordinate with SEs on maintenance windows.
- Post-hotfix audit: onboard a telemetry dashboard showing number of replay events, tombstone deletions detected, and tenants flagged. Link to investigation doc and incident timeline.

Artifacts and links:
- Incident timeline & postmortem: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/ONPREM-Upgrade-Tombstone-Incident-2026-03
- Reproduction harness (staging): https://github.com/redwood-inference/onprem-upgrade-sim
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/1892
- Runbook adjustments: gdrive:/Redwood/Runbooks/OnPremUpgradeQuiesce.md
comments:
2026-03-02 - Arielle Cheng: Initial triage complete. Verified logs from customer cluster show tombstone sweeper triggered at 03:12 UTC while helm post-upgrade hook still running. Notified SEs and scheduled hotfix window.

2026-03-04 - Mateo Ruiz: Implemented GC-disable flag and added a safety gate in the upgrade sequencer. Ran manual validation on staging cluster: helm upgrade -> operator quiesce -> post-upgrade reconcile succeeded. Preparing hotfix PR.

2026-03-06 - PR review: @Lina Patel requested stronger audit trail (annotation + event) for any replayed resource. Added annotation replay.origin=opera.replay.v1 and replay.timestamp. Also added metric operator.replay.count.

2026-03-09 - QA: Chaos test uncovered an edge case where replay attempted to re-create a CR owned by a different controller; added ownerReference verification and abort with alert instead of blind re-create.

2026-03-11 - Customer comms: SEs sent maintenance notice to affected customers for hotfix window 2026-03-13 01:00-03:00 UTC. Prepared rollback instructions (helm rollback + operator restart + manual reapply script).

2026-03-12 - Mateo Ruiz: Deployed operator-2026.03-hotfix-01 to staging and two pilot customer clusters. Monitoring shows no additional tombstone deletions during upgrade. Next: broader rollout and follow-up telemetry dashboard (ENG-782010).
